note: The Climb: ten real buildings in floor order, against the floors the child has ridden under power. Every quote below was fetched from the url beside it. The runtime gate is src/climb.js loadClimb(), which uses the same src/gate.js the fact bank uses. Two claims from the first draft were re-sourced rather than softened before they shipped: the Petronas deck parity (lower deck even, upper deck odd) and the Shanghai Tower speed record with the year it ended, both now carried by a verbatim quote. Past the last rung the ladder counts Burj Khalifas, so the roof card can never run out of a next thing to name.

items.name: the E. V. Haughwout Building
items.line: Only five storeys — and the world's first successful passenger lift went in here on 23 March 1857, a hydraulic lift designed for the building by Elisha Graves Otis. It rose about two-thirds of a foot every second.

sources.title: E. V. Haughwout Building — Wikipedia
sources.quote: installed the world's first successful passenger elevator on March 23, 1857, a hydraulic lift designed for the building by Elisha Graves Otis

items.name: the Flatiron Building
items.line: Its lifts were hydraulic — water pressure, not a motor at the top — right up to 1997, when new electric cars replaced the last hydraulic lifts in New York City.

sources.title: Flatiron Building — Wikipedia
sources.quote: replacing the antiquated cabs, which were the last hydraulic elevators in New York City

items.name: the Woolworth Building
items.line: Sixty storeys in 1913, served by 26 Otis gearless traction lifts — some express, running non-stop between chosen floors, some local, stopping at every floor in their range.

sources.title: Woolworth Building — Wikipedia
sources.quote: 26 Otis electric elevators with gearless traction, as well as an electric-drum shuttle elevator within the tower

items.name: the Shard
items.line: Seventy-two habitable floors inside a 95-storey tower, with 36 lifts. Not every storey is a floor you can stand on: the spire above the viewing gallery is storeys with nothing in them.

items.name: the Petronas Towers
items.line: The main lifts are double-deckers — two cars stacked in one shaft. The lower deck serves the even-numbered floors and the upper deck the odd ones, so you take an escalator up one level to board the top car.

sources.title: Petronas Towers — Wikipedia
sources.quote: All main lifts are double-decker with the lower deck of the lift taking passengers to even-numbered floors and upper deck to odd-numbered floors.

items.name: Taipei 101
items.line: Its observatory lifts climb at 16.83 metres every second — the fastest in the world when the tower opened in 2004, and fifth floor to eighty-ninth floor in 37 seconds.

sources.title: Taipei 101 — Wikipedia
sources.quote: 60.6 kilometers (37.7 mi) per hour, 16.83 m (55.22 ft) per second

items.name: the Empire State Building
items.line: One hundred and two storeys, and 73 lifts in all counting the service ones. The originals were designed to run at 1,200 feet a minute, but a city law held them to 700 until it was lifted just after the building opened.

sources.title: Empire State Building — Wikipedia
sources.quote: 73 elevators in all, including service elevators

items.name: the Willis Tower
items.line: You do not ride one lift to the top. Express lifts run to sky lobbies at the 33rd/34th and 66th/67th floors, and there you change to a local lift — like changing trains, but upwards.

sources.title: Willis Tower — Wikipedia
sources.quote: sky lobbies at the 33rd/34th and 66th/67th floors, where passengers could transfer to local elevators

items.name: the Shanghai Tower
items.line: Its lifts ran at 20.5 metres a second — the fastest in the world until 2017, when the Guangzhou CTF Finance Centre passed them at 21 metres a second.

sources.title: Shanghai Tower — Wikipedia
sources.quote: The Shanghai Tower also had the world's fastest elevators at a top speed of 20.5 meters per second (74 kilometers per hour; 46 miles per hour) until 2017

items.name: the Burj Khalifa
items.line: One hundred and fifty-four floors above the ground, and the longest lift travel in the world: 504 metres in one shaft. Ride this many floors again and you have climbed it twice.

sources.title: Burj Khalifa — Wikipedia
sources.quote: World's longest travel distance elevators: 504 m (1,654 ft)
